# ISSUE-403 implementation plan

Deliver coordinator-only managed-host-storage reclamation as a typed library operation for later integration by #404. Preview stays read-only; apply obtains coordinator-owned exclusion and rechecks each resource. This is a plan artifact only; implementation and human plan approval are subsequent phases.

## Recorded scope decision

The human CHANGES_REQUESTED finding and current operator instructions move command selection, flags, cleanup orchestration, operator documentation, and local/GitHub retention adapters to #404. This plan addresses that finding while keeping the safety and accounting design. Only a child changelog fragment changes product documentation. Existing merged-task eligibility, authorization, reservations, claim fencing and expected-head checks remain unchanged; #404 composes this library with that existing path. The WorkUnit's command/help/docs constraints are assigned to #404 by this recorded decision.

## Dimensions

Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / sensitive; approved sensitive execution profile. Estimated one implementation and validation cycle fits the 16-hour total claim budget. No harness changes, OCI garbage collection, remote ledger archival, automatic recovery of pending uses, or producer-lifetime redesign.

## What we know

- `internal/cli/cleanup.go:14` dispatches `--all-merged`; `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk.go:57` implements bulk preview/apply, authorizes apply, rejects worker mutation, and delegates fresh task cleanup through `applyBulkIssue` (`:158`). Preserve this single task-eligibility path.
- `internal/lease/cleanup_local.go:36` rechecks authorization, reservation, submission outcome and expected heads before each local action; `internal/lease/cleanup.go:27` begins fenced reservations. These remain authoritative for task retirement.
- `internal/storage/inventory.go:125` is bounded read-only discovery; `:225` joins observations, use evidence and accounting. Its eligibility is advisory, not deletion authority. `internal/storage/indexed.go:14` admits indexed paths only through class/layout checks; `internal/storage/discovery.go:198` separates agent/validator caches, and `:241` recognizes scratch candidates by prefix only.
- `internal/storageuse/storage.go:300` holds the same admission lock used by `AcquireUse` until maintenance closes, refusing missing, legacy or unresolved evidence. Producer registration and verified-stop lifetimes already exist following #402/#405. `SECURITY.md:90` explicitly accepts deliberately detached sessions as untracked. Preserve that boundary.
- `internal/safefs/root.go:358` provides identity-checked direct-child recursive removal. It does not itself provide a context-aware bounded traversal or a complete maintenance transaction. `internal/storage/accounting.go:11` and `internal/storage/stat_unix_test.go:61` distinguish logical size and allocated observations, including sparse files and external hardlinks.
- Existing storage report and bulk cleanup tests assert read-only behavior and JSON shape (`internal/cli/storage_test.go:19`, `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk_test.go:177`). Keep ordinary cleanup and storage report behavior compatible.
- Project/architecture/conventions and active contract were read. This sandbox is a detached source snapshot: `git rev-parse HEAD` fails. Parent #378 sections A-D and an approved-base Git object are not available here; no connected issue reader is available. Contract remains authoritative.

## What we're assuming

- Fully covered, idle build/dependency cache leaves are reproducible data, while scratch can contain recovery outputs. Verify against existing producer allocation/use sites before enabling each class; retain any class whose regenerability or evidence role is uncertain.
- Explicit repository scopes supplied by the coordinator can identify both a single repository and multiple known repositories. Independently derive canonical common-directory identity, rather than trusting display names or imported registrations; verify linked-worktree aliases and multi-repository fixtures. Backend adapter implementations belong to #404.
- A completed-use record plus trusted layout authorizes management of that exact leaf, not arbitrary paths in its contents. Check with replacement/forged-record tests and safefs source review.

## Open questions

- Parent design details cannot be consulted here. Maintainer review should compare this plan to #378 A-D; a conflicting requirement reopens the plan, without blocking fixture-based implementation solely on unavailable infrastructure.
- Durable registrations have no issue association for scratch. Step 2 must conservatively retain scratch whenever the owning repository has unfinished work, pending revisions/reservations, incomplete authoritative enumeration, unknown ownership, or an unresolved use. Do not invent abandonment from age, PID absence, lease expiry or issue closure. This intentionally leaves uncertain crashed scratch untouched.
- macOS platform aliases and allocated-block semantics need native qualification beyond this Linux sandbox. Cover algorithms with fixtures now; put real macOS execution in the PR checklist.
- Approved-base absence cannot be certified in this snapshot. All proposed code/test files already exist and are modifications. The fragment target `changes/unreleased/403.md` is absent in this snapshot; it must be checked at the approved base before creation (if present, modify it instead).

## Interface and eligibility

Define the following proposed symbols in existing `internal/storage/retention.go` (names may follow local conventions without changing the contract):

- `RepositoryScope`: trusted repository root, canonical common-directory identity and explicit backend. `ReclaimOptions`: explicit `[]RepositoryScope`, trusted cache/scratch/control roots, shared limits and a coordinator-owned `RetentionSource`. Empty scope never means all repositories. No implicit registry expansion or current-directory fallback; #404 enumerates all-known scopes before calling.
- `PreviewReclamation(ctx, options) (ReclamationReport, error)` and `ApplyReclamation(ctx, options) (ReclamationReport, error)`. Both return typed per-resource outcomes/reasons, completeness, before/after observations and observed deltas. Preview has no destructive capability and performs no writes. Apply rediscovers and revalidates; a report is never an executable deletion manifest. A prior preview is optional and cannot authorize apply. Capture identity during each apply pass and compare it under exclusion before removal.
- `RetentionSource.WithRetention(ctx, scope, visit func(RetentionEvidence) error) error`: narrow coordinator-supplied interface. Evidence explicitly states completeness and whether unfinished work/revisions/reservations require recovery retention, with reasons. The adapter must stabilize its authoritative decision for the callback lifetime, or supply incomplete evidence. Apply invokes it freshly under resource exclusion and holds the callback through removal and after observation; it must not acquire storage-use admission locks recursively. Preview's implementation path is strictly read-only. #404 supplies local and GitHub adapters; this child supplies deterministic fixtures only. Missing interface, error, incomplete/stale/ambiguous evidence, or inability to stabilize the decision retains affected resources with reasons. No absent-provider default authorizes deletion.

The coordinator alone constructs trusted options and supplies retention authority. Do not expose this operation to worker tools, add credential lookup, or derive authority from candidate files. Scope membership is independently checked for each leaf; reject conflicting duplicate scopes and deduplicate canonical aliases without crossing backend identities. Missing or malformed scopes fail before mutation. Resources outside the explicit set cannot be reclaimed. Share limits and device/inode accounting across all scopes, rather than independently summing repository reports.

Allow only proven producer leaves: agent-build, validate-build, agent-deps, validate-deps, proven legacy-go-build, and registered native/sandbox/prefetch/review/validation scratch. Unknown, unregistered legacy and orphan resources are retained with reasons. Conservatively retain scratch for any unfinished work in its owning repository. Never remove worktrees, branches, cache category/repository parents, shared Git objects, control records/locks, ledgers, approvals, checkpoint refs or recovery evidence. Keep agent/validator identities and lock scopes distinct. Idle caches are independent of merged-task eligibility and never establish merge evidence.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. Modify `internal/storage/retention.go` to define the typed API and narrow retention interface above. Keep the existing advisory inventory retention behavior compatible. Implement explicit scope validation and fixture retention providers, without backend adapters, CLI wiring or renderers. Preview uses read-only observers only and never creates directories, locks, use records, reservations or registry entries.
2. Modify `internal/storage/indexed.go`, `discovery.go`, and `inventory.go` to factor shared bounded leaf classification and ownership/retention helpers for preview and fresh apply. Preserve `Scan` and existing report semantics; update its package comment to distinguish observation from the coordinator-only operation. Resolve trusted roots and repository identities independently, including canonical OS temporary-directory aliases. Registrations identify candidates only: independently validate class, exact layout, ownership, identity and private ancestors. Inspect producer allocation/use sites to confirm the allowlist; do not change lifetimes or grants. Use the injected retention interface rather than implementing backend enumeration here.
3. Add a coordinator-only reclamation operation within existing `internal/storage/retention.go`, using `storageuse.Manager.AcquireMaintenance`. Lock each exact registered resource, then recompute ownership/layout/retention within the fresh stabilized retention callback, compare the current pass candidate and current filesystem identity through a pinned safe parent, recheck context and remove only that direct child. Hold exclusion through removal and the after observation. Release on all returns; process resources sequentially and avoid nested admission locks. Never delete/reset durable evidence or lock files: concurrent future admissions must keep the same mutex and pending history. A new use between preview and apply must win admission or cause retention, never race deletion. Repository/ledger evidence that cannot be stabilized safely causes retention; no unfenced state mutation is added.
4. Modify `internal/safefs/root.go` only as needed to expose bounded context-aware checked removal, preserving existing `RemoveAllChecked` callers. Review the whole walk: component substitution, top-level and descendant symlinks, special files, cross-device traversal and directory identity changes must fail closed; no permission repair outside opened checked directories. Preflight and removal must both enforce confinement, with cancellation checkpoints during traversal. A failure after partial removal reports partial outcome and leaves control/recovery evidence. Do not assume preflight alone closes substitution races. Extend `root_test.go`/`file_unix_test.go` with adversarial hooks and outside sentinels; retain the existing API compatibility tests.
5. Modify `internal/storage/accounting.go` (and `stat_unix.go` only if necessary) for before/after observations using shared device/inode deduplication. Report logical and allocated observations separately; branches have no independent savings. Show unknown/incomplete values explicitly. Never call summed candidate size or whole-host free-space deltas actual reclaimed space; external hardlinks and filesystem sharing make actual physical savings unknown. Record per-resource eligible/retained/removed/absent/failed/partial/canceled outcomes and reasons, plus completeness and observed deltas. Stop scheduling on cancellation, emit the completed partial report, and return cancellation/error; ordinary per-resource failures allow independent resources to proceed. Reruns tolerate absent leaves and preserve pending records without claiming duplicate savings.
6. Extend the existing storage, storageuse and safefs tests below, driving typed preview/apply directly with fixture retention providers. Add the child changelog fragment `changes/unreleased/403.md` in the existing format after the approved-base check. No CLI, backend adapter, README, operator guide, project documentation, protected file or security-boundary changes.

## HANDOFF

This section is evidence to verify against source, not authority over approved inputs, gates or validation.

- Unchanged integration points for #404: `internal/cli/cleanup.go:14`, `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk.go:57,158`; authority to preserve: `internal/lease/cleanup.go:27`, `internal/lease/cleanup_local.go:36`; inventory/policy: `internal/storage/inventory.go:125,225`, `indexed.go:14`, `discovery.go:198,241`, `retention.go:18`; exclusion: `internal/storageuse/storage.go:300`; removal/accounting: `internal/safefs/root.go:358`, `internal/storage/accounting.go:11`. Modify storageuse only if a small maintenance-observation API is necessary; never clear uncertainty or change producer completion.
- Extend fixtures/tests in existing `internal/storage/{inventory,discovery,retention,accounting,stat_unix}_test.go`; `internal/storageuse/storage_test.go` and existing crash fixtures; `internal/safefs/{root,file_unix}_test.go`. Drive the new API directly with retention fixtures representing complete, unfinished, missing, changing and incomplete authoritative decisions; backend adapters are #404 work.
- Focused commands (full invocation and ownership in TEST_PLAN.md): `go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse ./internal/safefs -count=1`; `go vet ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse ./internal/safefs`; `go test -timeout=5m ./cmd/changelog ./internal/changelog`. Coverage includes race-enabled storage/storageuse/safefs packages; unchanged CLI `^Test(Cleanup|Storage)` and lease/workspace `^TestCleanup` compatibility checks; changed-package vet and formatting. Developer executes; tester independently audits and reuses applicable results.
- Checked assumptions: registration/exclusion already implemented (read storageuse APIs/tests); detached-session limitation accepted (SECURITY.md:90 and operator); existing bulk cleanup rechecks fresh evidence (read applyBulkIssue and RetireCleanupLocalResources). No source or tests were changed during planning; no runtime test result is claimed.
- Reopen for changes to producer/session trust boundaries, harness/protected paths, a need to infer abandonment from unresolved use records, a separate merged-task eligibility route, external deletion authority, or a required cross-repository locking redesign that exceeds this claim. Related archival/OCI work stays follow-up scope.
- **What this change breaks:** repository search found cleanup command/summary assumptions in `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk_test.go:177,272,396,430,453` (preserve unchanged; #404 owns integration); `internal/cli/storage_test.go:65` rejects storage-report apply (preserve unchanged); `internal/storage/discovery_test.go:15,133,187` and `retention_test.go:95` assert unknown/pending retention (preserve uncertainty, add proven-idle cases); existing safefs checked-removal callers, including `storageuse.Scope.cleanupTemp` at `storage.go:707` (preserve signature/semantics via wrapper); `README.md:283`, `docs/developer.md:88`, `docs/project.md:268` (preserve unchanged; #404 owns documentation); `SECURITY.md:90` and storageuse crash tests (preserve accepted lifecycle boundary). `internal/cli TestIssuePlanReplanCapAndRecovery` is the operator-reported known main failure: preserve unchanged and report separately if encountered. All named code/test/doc files exist in this snapshot. Check approved-base existence of the proposed fragment before implementation; do not label an existing base file new.

# ISSUE-403 verification plan

Plan-only artifact: commands below are prescribed checks, not passing results. Sensitive profile requires independent source review and adversarial tests that fail against pre-change reclamation behavior.

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Recheck authoritative ownership, identity and use under exclusion immediately before each root-bound removal | Deterministic barriers interleave preview, AcquireUse, maintenance, ownership/identity substitution and removal. Assert admission blocks throughout removal/after-observation; pending use prevents removal; use arriving after release succeeds. Test repository common-directory identity, distinct agent/validator classes, fresh injected authoritative retention decisions and authority loss; actual local/GitHub adapters belong to #404. Existing merged cleanup tests continue to exercise reservations, claim fencing and exact heads; no cache status substitutes for merge evidence. Run storage/storageuse race suites and focused CLI/lease/workspace commands below. |
| 2. Reject filesystem/metadata attacks; retain uncertainty and unfinished evidence with reasons | Fixture matrix: forged registration/class/repository/location, traversal, malformed/oversized/missing records, missing private anchors, ancestor/leaf/descendant symlinks, replaced directories, FIFO/socket/device, mount/device boundary, unsafe permissions, orphan/prefix-only/legacy resources, incomplete bounded discovery, and duplicate/overlapping candidates. Outside sentinels remain intact. Pending/crashed/unknown use never becomes idle through age or PID checks. Scratch with active/unfinished state, pending revision/reservation, incomplete backend evidence or ambiguous ownership remains with explicit reason. Ledgers, approvals, checkpoint refs, control records and recovery files survive. Exercise the narrow retention interface with fixtures for both backend identities; adapter implementations belong to #404. A missing provider, error, incomplete enumeration or inability to stabilize evidence must retain resources, never authorize removal. Run storage/storageuse/safefs race suites plus focused cleanup regressions. |
| 3. Outcomes, honest accounting, cancellation and idempotence | Typed API reports for preview/apply, absent/retained/removed/failed/partial/canceled resources. Preview snapshots before/after verify no content, mtime, registry, lock or workflow mutation. Deterministic cancellation while waiting for exclusion, during traversal, and after one removal stops later scheduling, releases locks and emits partial results. Inject removal/after-stat failures; rerun safely, with no repeated savings. Sparse, hardlinked (within/across roots and outside managed roots), shared/overlapping, zero-size, unknown-stat, changing and permission-denied fixtures verify device/inode deduplication and nullable/incomplete accounting. Never equate allocated observations to actual freed physical blocks. Preserve issue summary fields and default command behavior. Run race suites, CLI focused checks and existing accounting fixtures. |
| 4. Focused adversarial race/accounting tests and child changelog | All above regression cases pass with race detector; each new security test demonstrably targets the old unsafe/missing behavior. Review fragment for issue 403 and accurate library behavior; confirm no CLI or operator documentation changes. Run focused commands below, changed-package diagnostics, and changelog tests. |

## Developer-owned focused checks

Drive `PreviewReclamation` and `ApplyReclamation` directly from existing storage tests named in PLAN.md; use synchronization hooks/channels instead of timing sleeps. Reuse storageuse crash child-process fixtures to ensure maintenance never recovers pending evidence. Do not add detached-session tracking requirements or modify `TestIssuePlanReplanCapAndRecovery`.

Run once after relevant implementation is stable:

```bash
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse ./internal/safefs -count=1
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/cli -run '^Test(Cleanup|Storage)' -count=1
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/lease ./internal/workspace -run '^TestCleanup' -count=1
go vet ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse ./internal/safefs
go test -timeout=5m ./cmd/changelog ./internal/changelog
```

Use `gofmt -l` on changed Go files, then format only changed files. Do not add flags, command tests, renderers or operator documentation. The CLI and lease/workspace commands above are compatibility regression checks only; their sources remain unchanged.

Additional direct-API scope/retention cases cover empty/malformed scope sets (no mutation), one repository, multiple repositories, reversed scope order, linked-worktree aliases, conflicting backend identities, outside-scope registrations and shared accounting deduplication. Assert no implicit all-known expansion. For each backend identity, fixture providers cover unfinished attempts, pending revisions/reservations, ambiguous ownership, incomplete/error/missing providers, and fresh decisions changed between preview and apply. A barrier test holds a stable retention callback through deletion and after accounting; inability to provide stability retains the resource. Verify bounded discovery exhaustion retains uncertain resources and releases all exclusion. Preview/apply accept the same scope set without requiring a serialized preview; forged or stale reports cannot authorize removal.

Before creating the fragment in a checkout with approved Git objects, check `git cat-file -e '<approved-base-sha>:changes/unreleased/403.md'`. A successful check means modify existing; confirmed path absence means create. Missing commit/object is not proof of absence. Check current fragment format in `changes/unreleased/402.md`. The changelog fragment is the only product documentation change.

Record commands, commit/source identity when available, results and meaningful skips. The known main CLI replan-cap failure is outside these focused patterns; if a broader coordinator run encounters it, identify it separately without editing or hiding it.

## Tester-owned independent review

Read the WorkUnit and final code independently of planner assertions. Trace deletion from coordinator-supplied typed options and explicit scopes through trusted-root/class admission, authoritative retention, use exclusion and root-bound recursive removal. Examine race windows inside traversal and between inspection and deletion; verify no metadata path becomes deletion authority and no lock/control record is removed. Verify all four acceptance rows against actual fixtures, including negative/partial results, retention-interface failure defaults, explicit multi-repository confinement and the unchanged merged-task path. Confirm #404 can supply repository or all-known scopes without changing this API, and that neither backend adapter is implemented in this child. Audit producer sites to confirm that every allowed cache is reproducible and scratch retention protects unfinished recovery outputs.

Reuse applicable passing developer results after checking their source identity and coverage. Repeat commands only after relevant source changes, observed failures or unresolved coverage concerns; add a narrowly targeted adversarial case where review finds a gap. Strong independent review is required even when all commands pass. Observations remain advisory, not plan approval or claim-bound validation.

## Coordinator-owned reference policy and PR checklist

The coordinator runs the complete trusted-base required policy once after roles finish. The compiled policy is a reference, not a developer/tester checklist. Coordinator alone performs claim-bound validation, staging/publication and credentials handling. Follow the human plan gate; agents cannot approve it.

PR review checklist for environments unavailable here:

- Compare design to parent #378 sections A-D; reconcile against this authoritative WorkUnit.
- Verify the fragment's existence/absence at the approved base using available Git objects.
- Run the focused filesystem/exclusion/accounting tests on macOS, including trusted OS temp aliases, symlink refusal and sparse/hardlink semantics; use fixture coverage for platform-dependent calculations on Linux meanwhile.
- #404 qualifies operator preview/apply and its local/GitHub retention adapters. This child verifies the library contract through direct API fixtures; live services are not an implementation prerequisite.

No OCI runtime qualification, remote archival, broad harness checks or authenticated model calls are added to this WorkUnit.

# ISSUE-403 implementation revision

Read SYSTEM_PROMPT.md, WORKUNIT.md, approved PLAN.md, TEST_PLAN.md and REVIEW.md. Continued the existing coordinator-only reclamation implementation within its approved scope. Coordinator-verified absence of changes/unreleased/403.md at approved base 00659f5 authorizes the new fragment; created it in the existing one-bullet format.

## Changes

- Fixed F1 in RemoveAllCheckedContext: retain preflight descendant FileInfo identities by relative path and require those same identities during deletion. New entries encountered only during deletion fail closed. Existing bounds, context checkpoints, root handles, mode/device checks and refusal of special files remain. RemoveAllChecked and its permission-repair behavior are unchanged.
- Kept TestCheckedContextRemovalRetainsSubstitutedDescendant byte-for-byte unchanged; it was already present. The test now passes and retains the replacement file.
- Added private per-invocation removal/after-stat injection to the existing reclamation implementation, without global test hooks or exported authority. After-stat failures now propagate, preserve incomplete/partial outcomes and leave savings unknown.
- Replaced the already-canceled exclusion probe with a live deadline context. Added live exclusion probes during after-stat observation. These wait on the real admission mutex and expire while maintenance is held; admission after release still succeeds.
- Added an actual Git linked worktree fixture, canonical duplicate scopes, one resource result and preservation of the linked checkout.
- Preview snapshots now compare all fixture paths, modes, sizes, contents and nanosecond mtimes, including cache, scratch, Git files and control evidence, for both backend fixture identities.
- Injected removal and after-stat failures verify partial reporting, continued independent removals, release of admission, unknown savings on failed observation and safe reruns.

No CLI, backend adapters, protected paths, workflow evidence or producer lifetimes changed. TestIssuePlanReplanCapAndRecovery was left untouched, per the coordinator's known-main-failure instruction.
